cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: See What This Took
cards.instruction: Make someone recognize the courage, restraint, or emotional labor your choices required.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. I told the committee I couldn't chair another year. Please appreciate what those two sentences took. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Good. Could you stay on until we find someone?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. I rehearsed in your car until I stopped apologising. That wasn't me advertising a temporary vacancy.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then I'll tell them you're exhausted and need a break.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Please don't supply the excuse I spent an hour removing. Could you recognise a refusal I finally managed without one?

mechanism: An outgoing chair directs the handover but negotiates practical help so B recognizes the courage of a refusal without supplying an excuse.
confusable: Unlike simply insisting a boundary be obeyed, A wants the effort of saying no recognized; A offers an adjustment to keep B cooperating.
comparison: Public committee succession and an ally differ from a private apology recipient examining unsent anger.
seedUse: Use D105-b rehearsed refusal and unwanted excuse; S02-a adjusts arrangements while presenting control of the transition.
